title: Catch the ETL VM before it runs out of memory
skills: metric alert aggregation, window and frequency

ticket.from: Lena Brandt, data platform on-call lead
ticket.subject: vm-etl-02 crashed at 04:05 and nobody was paged
body: Last night `vm-etl-02` (the Linux VM that runs our Python ETL) ran out of memory: the loader leaks slowly all
evening, the kernel killed it at 04:05 and the VM rebooted. The morning loads were late and the first person
to notice was the finance team at 07:30. Tom had set up `etl-vm-memory-low` a while ago, but it never paged.
- **Fix Tom's rule, keep its name** (`etl-vm-memory-low`, our runbook links to it). It must page
`ag-data-oncall` (severity 2 or more urgent) at least 20 minutes before the crash, while there is still time to
restart the loader. The nightly batch at 01:00 briefly uses a lot of memory: that is normal and must not page.
- **Page when the VM is down**: a second rule on the VM's availability, severity 0 or 1, to `ag-data-oncall`,
within five minutes of the VM going down.
The metrics of the last 24 hours are in Azure Monitor (`az monitor metrics list`). When your rules are ready,
replay last night against them (`lab alerts replay`) and send me the output.
This is the lab's simulated subscription: nothing is sent to Azure.

acceptance.text: etl-vm-memory-low pages ag-data-oncall (sev 0-2) between 03:20 and 03:45, and stays silent during the 01:00 batch.

checks.fail: The memory alert would not have paged as the ticket asks:
Tom's rule etl-vm-memory-low was not fixed (it must keep its name).

acceptance.text: A rule on VmAvailabilityMetric pages ag-data-oncall (sev 0-1) within five minutes of the 04:05 crash.

checks.fail: The availability alert would not have paged as the ticket asks:

acceptance.text: You replayed last night against your rules after their last change.

checks.fail: The rules were not replayed after their last change.

hints: `az monitor metrics alert list -g rg-etl-prod -o table` shows Tom's rule: look at its threshold, aggregation, window and severity, and at who it notifies.
`az monitor metrics list --resource vm-etl-02 --metric "Available Memory Bytes" --interval 15m` shows the leak and the 01:00 batch. Memory is in bytes: 1 GiB is 1073741824.
The lab's `az monitor metrics alert update` does not change a condition: delete the rule and create it again with the same name.
A threshold that is too high also catches the 01:00 batch; one that is too low (or a long window) pages after the crash. A 15-minute average smooths the noise.
VmAvailabilityMetric is 1 while the VM is up and 0 while it is down: `avg VmAvailabilityMetric < 1` over 5 minutes catches the reboot; `max` over the same window would not.
`lab alerts replay` prints when each rule would have fired last night: run it after your last change.

Available Memory Bytes.description: Memory available to applications (16 GiB VM)

Percentage CPU.description: The percentage of allocated compute units in use by the VM

VmAvailabilityMetric.description: 1 while the VM is up, 0 while it is not available

setup: az monitor metrics alert create -n etl-vm-memory-low -g rg-etl-prod --scopes vm-etl-02 --condition "avg Available Memory Bytes < 500000000" --window-size 5m --evaluation-frequency 5m --severity 3 --description "Tom: memory low on the ETL VM"

reference.infra: az monitor metrics alert list -g rg-etl-prod -o table
az monitor metrics list --resource vm-etl-02 --metric "Available Memory Bytes" --interval 15m
az monitor metrics alert delete -n etl-vm-memory-low -g rg-etl-prod

az monitor metrics alert create -n etl-vm-memory-low -g rg-etl-prod --scopes vm-etl-02 --condition "avg Available Memory Bytes < 1073741824" --window-size 15m --evaluation-frequency 5m --severity 2 --action ag-data-oncall --description "The ETL loader is leaking: restart it before the VM runs out of memory"

az monitor metrics alert create -n etl-vm-unavailable -g rg-etl-prod --scopes vm-etl-02 --condition "avg VmAvailabilityMetric < 1" --window-size 5m --evaluation-frequency 1m --severity 1 --action ag-data-oncall --description "vm-etl-02 is down"
